input:
Vad ska den nya fabriken i Helsingborg tillverka? Den ska producera förpackade färdigrätter för den svenska dagligvaruhandeln. Det svenska livsmedelsföretaget Solfis invigde anläggningen på tisdagen. De första leveranserna till butiker planeras till nästa månad.

Produktionen startar med en linje för kylda färdigrätter. Under hösten ska en andra linje tas i drift, förutsatt att provkörningarna går enligt plan. Fabriken har anställt 45 personer inför starten. Enligt Solfis kan ytterligare ett tjugotal jobb tillkomma när båda linjerna är i gång.

Industrirobotar ska packa färdiga tråg i kartonger och stapla dem på pallar. Personalen ansvarar bland annat för råvarumottagning och kvalitetskontroller. Det svenska bioteknikföretaget Flonletron ska analysera hållbarheten hos de första produktionsserierna.

Det svenska energiföretaget Hascuhent har levererat ett system som återvinner värme från kylningen och använder den för att förvärma vatten till rengöringen. Hur mycket energi systemet sparar ska följas upp under fabrikens första hela driftår.

Produktionsdata ska lagras i molnlagringstjänsten Flomsova Cloud, en produkt från det svenska analysföretaget Flomsova AB i Linköping. Det finländska mjukvaruföretaget Disgova Foods Oyj har levererat ett system för orderhantering och leveransplanering. Lösningen bygger delvis på teknik som används i betalappar, men i fabriken används den för att bekräfta leveranser, inte för att hantera betalningar.

input:
At a Seattle waterfront corner on Tuesday morning, a rider folded an e-scooter and carried it into a café as the first ferry commuters walked past. That short trip from the waterfront to a nearby stop is the kind of journey a new visitor guide will help people plan.

Mefix AB, a Swedish travel company, has awarded a contract to Brufia Foods, a United Kingdom gaming company, to build an interactive guide for visitors spending a day in Seattle. Brerhyn LLC, a United States gaming company, will handle local testing under the contract.

The guide will let visitors compare walking routes with trips on e-scooters and see where they can park before continuing on foot. Early testing will focus on the waterfront and downtown, where steep streets and busy crossings can make a route that looks short on a map take longer than expected.

The companies did not disclose the value of the contract. A trial version is expected ahead of the summer travel season, with feedback from residents and visitors used to revise the routes before a wider release.

Ebba Mamdardson, kommunalråd i Umeå, ser kapitalrundan i Krantex AB som ett test på om stadens logistikföretag kan växa utan att flytta verksamheten söderut. Det svenska logistikbolaget har tagit in 64 miljoner kronor i en nyemission som leddes av en investerare från Stockholm. Enligt villkoren betalas 48 miljoner kronor ut vid tillträdet. Resten betalas ut när bolaget har öppnat en andra omlastningspunkt och tecknat två fleråriga kundavtal.

Krantex AB samordnar leveranser åt mindre och medelstora företag som inte fyller en lastbil på egen hand. Pengarna ska gå till terminalutrustning och fler fasta avgångar mellan Umeå och Stockholm. Den första nya kvällsavgången planeras till hösten. Tanken är att kunderna ska kunna lämna gods senare på dagen utan att leveransen förskjuts ett dygn.

Det svenska livsmedelsföretaget Dronfluskar Works AB deltar i ett pilotprojekt för kylda leveranser, medan de svenska modeföretagen Plofix AB och Borum testar gemensam returfrakt. Det svenska medieföretaget Suhëszora AB prövar samma linje för distribution av trycksaker. Pilotavtalen löper i sex månader och innehåller inga garantier om fortsatta volymer. Svenska Relflaglum AB, som också verkar inom logistik, sköter den lokala utkörningen i Stockholm under försöksperioden.

Nils Trobix, analytiker, bedömer att fyllnadsgraden på returerna norrut blir viktigare för lönsamheten än antalet nya kunder. En full bil söderut räcker inte om den går halvtom tillbaka. Han pekar också på att kyltransporterna kräver separat utrustning, vilket begränsar hur fritt bolaget kan fördela godset mellan avgångarna. Någon värdering offentliggörs inte.

Husfa Partners Ltd, a United Kingdom software company, announced a partnership Tuesday with regional equipment distributors to test a shared inventory system for battery packs, solar panels and drones.

The pilot will begin in Dublin and Copenhagen before expanding to Oslo and Edinburgh. The software will let participating distributors check stock at other warehouses before ordering replacement equipment, a step intended to reduce delivery delays and unnecessary shipments.

Greta Stantreoström, head of sales, said the first phase would focus on whether warehouse staff could rely on stock counts from other sites. David Mambardez, also a head of sales, said the partners would review delivery times and order accuracy before deciding whether to extend the arrangement.

Omar Nenlarberg, a spokesperson, said the partners had not disclosed the value of the agreement or committed to a wider rollout. He said each distributor would continue to set its own prices and handle its own orders.

Mats Fasja, a mayor, welcomed the trial but said any gains should be measured against the cost of training staff. Henrik Hilcovaez, a union representative, said workers should be consulted before the system changes how warehouse shifts are organised.

För svenska industriföretag som vill automatisera delar av sin verksamhet är det ofta lättare att visa att en robot fungerar än att visa att den lönar sig. I ett pilotprojekt kan arbetsflödet anpassas efter tekniken. När samma lösning ska in i den dagliga driften måste den däremot fungera med befintliga rutiner, skiftbyten och ojämna varuflöden. Det är steget från pilot till reguljär drift som den svenska robotikverksamheten bakom flazeo.se nu tar in kapital för att finansiera.

Rundan på 38 miljoner kronor leds av två privata investerare, med deltagande från befintliga ägare. Merparten av kapitalet ska gå till installationer och service, snarare än till att bredda produktutbudet. I Jönköping ska verksamheten bygga upp ett team som kan driftsätta systemen hos kunder och utbilda personalen på plats. En mindre del av kapitalet avsätts för att pröva efterfrågan i Köpenhamn, där lastcyklar ingår i de leveransflöden som verksamheten vill anpassa sin teknik till.

Det svenska modeföretaget Borum AB deltar i ett pilotprojekt för att sortera returer, medan det svenska gruvföretaget Dakix utvärderar tekniken för intern materialhantering. För Greta Kreflardton, som är kund, är det viktigaste måttet hur ofta personalen behöver avbryta sitt ordinarie arbete för att hjälpa roboten. David Sunplexmann, försäljningschef för verksamheten bakom flazeo.se, räknar med att resultat från hela arbetsskift blir viktigare i kommande kundsamtal än robotens kapacitet i en enskild uppgift.

Nästa milstolpe är att få de första pilotprojekten att övergå i fleråriga serviceavtal. Först då går det att bedöma om intäkterna från en installation täcker kostnaden för att hålla den i drift.

”Vi har återställt betalningarna i butikerna, men näthandeln är fortfarande stängd”, sade Alice Drokis, vd för Derkon, strax före börsstängning.

Den svenska detaljhandelskedjans aktie stängde 4,3 procent lägre efter att ett IT-intrång tvingat bolaget att pausa nätförsäljningen under större delen av handelsdagen. Kursen återhämtade sig något mot slutet av handeln när bolaget meddelade att kunder åter kunde betala med kort i samtliga butiker. Derkon lämnade ingen prognos för när nätbutiken öppnar och uppgav att det ännu är för tidigt att beräkna försäljningsbortfallet.

Lisa Krogeoström, teknikchef på Derkon, sade att de berörda systemen hade isolerats och att utredningen ännu inte kunnat fastställa om kunduppgifter hade röjts. Bolaget uppgav att redan lagda beställningar kan bli försenade.

Bland de svenska energibolagen steg Plurzomskeo AB med 0,6 procent efter att ha bekräftat sin produktionsprognos. Aktien i bolaget bakom corsta.se backade 0,4 procent när lägre elpriser pressade flera elproducenter. Inget av energibolagen rapporterade driftstörningar.

Det breda marknadsindexet slutade 0,2 procent lägre. För Derkon blir nästa besked om nätbutiken avgörande för hur mycket av den uteblivna försäljningen som kan tas igen före helgen.

Oslo, 14 January 2026 — A backlog at a freight terminal outside Oslo is holding up everything from network cabinets to prefabricated stair treads. A stretch of freezing rain slowed arrivals last week, but the weather has cleared and the queue has not. The problem now is finding enough trucks to move several days’ worth of freight at once.

For Swedish telecom company Zilzex, the delay means installation crews may reach customer sites before their equipment does. Swedish construction company Varhomdria faces the reverse problem: a shipment could arrive after the crane booked to unload it has moved to another job. In both cases, the cost of a late delivery depends less on the value of the cargo than on what was scheduled around it.

Maria Cemskisström, a chief technology officer, said a tracking update is useful only if it gives a dispatcher time to change the plan. The Gläjoskia Track parcel-tracking service can show when a consignment was last scanned, but that scan cannot tell a site manager when another truck will be available. The Gläjoskia Mail email service can carry a revised delivery notice; someone still has to make the call to rebook the crew.

Buyers in Zurich may be tempted to pay for faster freight. For the most time-sensitive loads, that may make sense. For the rest, the better bargain could be a delivery window wide enough to absorb a missed connection. A day of slack looks expensive on a spreadsheet until it costs less than a crane standing idle.

input:
Why are a Swedish construction company, a Swiss telecom company and a U.S. fashion company all looking at Austin? Each sees a different opening in the same market: building out commercial space, connecting businesses and selling clothes designed for the working day.

Dragex Foods AB, the Swedish construction company, is starting with commercial renovations rather than pursuing large new developments. Smaller projects offer a way to build relationships with local contractors and learn what clients expect before taking on more complex work.

Zorjóflyn is taking a similarly focused approach. The Swiss telecom company plans to start with connectivity services for small businesses, including teams developing fintech apps. Its first test will be whether it can offer reliable service and responsive support to customers that don’t have large technology teams of their own.

Zorlanskárd Corp. is using Austin to test demand for workwear that can move between job sites and customer-facing settings. Rather than committing to a permanent store at the outset, Zorlanskárd plans to use temporary retail spaces to see which fits and fabrics shoppers return for.

Mayor Julia Kralmera said the more telling measure of the expansion would be how much work the newcomers put in the hands of local suppliers and contractors. For now, the thing to watch is whether those first projects, service contracts and retail trials lead to repeat business.

input:
Mia Stonmia, head of sales, spent a morning in Manchester asking building managers what would make them switch suppliers of smart meters. The answer had less to do with the price of the hardware than with who would pick up the phone when a meter stopped sending readings.

That distinction is shaping a supplier’s expansion from London into Manchester. Rather than opening a showroom or hiring a full sales team, it is starting with a small group of commercial landlords. The first installations will test whether the supplier can serve buildings with several tenants without leaving property managers to untangle billing queries themselves.

Anna Florkumström, a spokesperson, said the initial offer would bundle installation and support into a single price, so landlords could compare it with the cost of keeping their existing meters. The approach is a departure from the pricing familiar to customers of budget airlines, where a low headline fare can give way to a longer list of charges. For a landlord signing a multiyear contract, the cost of a return visit can matter more than a discount on the meter.

The expansion also poses a staffing question. Sending technicians from London avoids the cost of hiring before orders are secure, but it makes a short service call expensive. Maria Zolbrynez, a spokesperson, said the supplier would track how often technicians had to return to a site before deciding whether to base a crew in Manchester.

For Stonmia, the clearest sign of demand will come after the first bills go out. A landlord willing to try a meter in one building is useful; one willing to order for the rest of a portfolio could justify a local team.

input:
„Mit der Eröffnung in Düsseldorf rücken Fertigung und Qualitätsprüfung unter ein Dach“, sagte die Werksleitung bei der Inbetriebnahme der neuen Fabrik. Dort sollen zunächst Drohnen für die Inspektion von Gebäuden und Industrieanlagen montiert werden. Die Produktion startet in kleinen Serien. Erst wenn die Abläufe in Montage und Endprüfung eingespielt sind, soll die Stückzahl steigen.

Der deutsche Versicherer Flisplyn deckt Risiken aus dem laufenden Betrieb ab. Das deutsche Energieunternehmen, das unter ir@jonlix.de erreichbar ist, liefert Strom für die Fertigung. Das deutsche Sicherheitsunternehmen Brezum AG übernimmt die Zutrittskontrolle und sichert die Anlieferung.

Für die regionale Zulieferindustrie ist vor allem der schrittweise Hochlauf interessant: Gehäuseteile und Verpackungen sollen möglichst aus der Umgebung bezogen werden. Ob daraus längerfristige Aufträge entstehen, hängt davon ab, wie viele Geräte das Werk nach der Anlaufphase zuverlässig ausliefern kann. Angaben zur geplanten Jahresproduktion und zur Zahl der Arbeitsplätze machte die Werksleitung bei der Eröffnung nicht.

A U.S. mining company has launched the Trohix Drive app, a fleet-tracking product for monitoring vehicles at mine sites. The launch puts a routine but costly problem in focus: when a haul truck sits idle or takes longer than expected to complete a run, dispatchers need to know whether the delay is isolated or part of a wider bottleneck.

The app’s value will depend less on how many vehicles it can display than on whether dispatchers can use that information to shorten queues and keep loads moving. Patchy connectivity at remote sites could limit its usefulness, and a location feed alone cannot tell a supervisor whether a truck has stopped because of a breakdown, a safety check or a queue at the loading point.

Unlike solar panels, whose output can be measured directly, or plant-based burgers, whose sales offer a quick read on customer demand, fleet software is harder to evaluate in isolation. Fuel use and turnaround times can improve because routes get shorter or workloads change, even if the app makes little difference. A convincing test would compare similar shifts and account for those changes. For the mining company, that evidence would matter more than the number of vehicles it signs up.

Emma Senkera, Technikchefin der Biljon AG, will vom Standort Frankfurt aus einen Markt erschließen, in dem Funklöcher nicht nur lästig sind, sondern Lieferungen verzögern können. Der deutsche Telekommunikationsanbieter plant, vernetzte Logistik für Lebensmittelhändler in den Vereinigten Staaten anzubieten. Als erster Abnehmer ist das US-Lebensmittelunternehmen Gekromplard vorgesehen. Ob daraus ein breiteres Geschäft wird, hängt davon ab, ob die Technik im Alltag mehr einspart, als ihre Einführung kostet.

Im Kern geht es darum, Kühltransporte auch dort im Blick zu behalten, wo die Verbindung zeitweise ausfällt. Das deutsche Bauunternehmen Brebreltyn bringt dafür die Flottenortungs-App Brebreltyn Drive ein. Sie soll Standortdaten bei einem Verbindungsabbruch zwischenspeichern und später übertragen. Das schließt Lücken in der Dokumentation, hilft aber wenig, wenn die Leitstelle sofort auf eine Störung reagieren muss. Genau dieser Unterschied dürfte für die Bewertung des Pilotprojekts entscheidend sein.

Bei Vorführungen in Dresden ging es auch um Geräte, die nicht zum Kernangebot gehören. Das deutsche Sicherheitsunternehmen Fufla zeigte das Fitness-Wearable Fufla Pulse. Für Anton Pelca, eine Kundin, die die Testanwendung aus Sicht der Beschäftigten beurteilte, stand dabei die Frage im Vordergrund, ob sich private Fitnessdaten von betrieblichen Informationen trennen lassen. Drohnen wurden als mögliche Ergänzung für Bestandskontrollen auf großen Betriebsgeländen diskutiert, sind aber für den Markteintritt nicht vorgesehen.

Ein Auftrag von Gekromplard würde der Biljon AG eine Referenz verschaffen, aber noch nicht zeigen, dass sich das Angebot auf andere Händler übertragen lässt. Entscheidend ist, wie viel Anpassung jede weitere Flotte erfordert. Muss die Technik für jeden Kunden neu eingerichtet werden, wächst mit dem Umsatz auch der Aufwand. Gelingt der Anschluss dagegen mit überschaubaren Änderungen, könnte aus dem Pilotprojekt ein Geschäft werden, das über den ersten Abnehmer hinausreicht.

input:
Zorjóflyn's new factory opened in Lyon on Tuesday, giving the Swiss telecom company its first production site in the city for equipment that connects office buildings and industrial sites to fibre networks.

The plant will assemble and test optical modules and network switches, with initial shipments expected later this year. Until now, the company has relied on contractors for final assembly. Bringing that work in-house will let engineers diagnose faults on the production line instead of sending failed units back to suppliers.

Parfar Inc., a U.S. biotech company, took part in a pre-opening trial that used the Parfar Mail email service, one of its products, to deliver test alerts from the Lyon factory to a support team in London. The trial checked whether those alerts still reached staff when the factory switched to a backup connection.

The factory will start with one assembly line. A second will be added if orders justify it. The company did not disclose the cost of the site or say how many units it expects to ship in its first year.

På kajen i Umeå drar en chaufför åt det sista spännbandet. På pallarna står kartonger med svenska havrekakor, på väg till de första provbutikerna i norra Finland.

För Cunskidyn AB är steget över Kvarken ett sätt att pröva en ny marknad utan att binda kapital i ett eget lager. Ett tiotal butiker får varorna i höst. Det är inte premiärleveransen som avgör om satsningen håller, utan om handlarna beställer igen när provsmakningen är över och kakorna ska bära sin egen hyllplats.

Finanschefen Paul Jamskikson pekar på frakten som den stora osäkerheten. En nästan tom lastbil kostar nästan lika mycket att skicka som en full. Därför samordnas leveranserna med andra exportörers, och transportören följer fordonen i Skurar Drive, appen för fordonsuppföljning från det svenska reseföretaget Skurar AB.

I samma del av Finland undersöker det amerikanska gruvbolaget bakom www.vomtrik.com möjligheten att köpa underhållstjänster lokalt. Gruvbolagets planer har inget med havrekakorna att göra, men båda satsningarna ger regionala leverantörer en chans att sälja på andra sidan vattnet.

För Umeåtrakten är det värt att hålla ögonen på returlasterna. Om åkarna hittar gods också på vägen hem blir det billigare för nästa lilla livsmedelsproducent att prova den finländska marknaden.

For several years, biotechnology company Gafik has coordinated shipments from its Stockholm office with suppliers and customers overseas. Staff use a shared scheduling portal to track deliveries, while the company posts public notices on www.gafik.se.

On Tuesday morning, Gafik took the scheduling portal offline after staff spotted delivery updates they had not made. A review found that an account belonging to a former contractor had been used overnight. The company said it had disabled the account and was checking whether anyone had viewed or copied customer records.

Mats Fasja, head of sales at Gafik, said staff called customers whose delivery instructions had changed and asked them to confirm the original details. Two shipments were held in Stockholm while the checks were carried out. Both were released by late afternoon, and neither contained temperature-sensitive material, he said.

Finnish retailer Remlesflora and U.S. biotechnology company Kezum were among the customers notified. The British operator of nordrevum.co.uk helped verify collection times against its dispatch records. U.S. telecom company Gempa Labs Inc. helped review connection records for a support line used by staff in Toronto. Gafik said it had found no evidence that the incident extended beyond the scheduling portal.

The company said the portal would stay offline until staff had reviewed all active accounts and checked recent changes to delivery instructions. Its public website remained available. In the meantime, customers expecting a shipment this week were advised to confirm any change by calling their usual contact rather than replying to a delivery notice.

Zurich, 17 March 2026 — Sukiå's new partnership with Rämhik Ltd will test whether the challenges and rewards that keep players coming back to games can also help travellers plan a trip. The two UK businesses announced a pilot in Zurich that will let customers earn booking credits by completing trip-planning tasks, such as putting together a weekend itinerary.

For Sukiå's travel business, the pilot is a chance to reach customers before they have settled on a destination or begun comparing prices. Rämhik will design the challenges and use the trial to see whether mechanics developed for games hold their appeal in a setting where customers may visit only a few times a year.

Founder Omar Zertriamann said repeat visits would matter less than whether customers returned with a clearer idea of what they wanted to book. The partners plan to track completed itineraries and bookings alongside the cost of the credits, a measure that will help them distinguish new sales from discounts for customers who would have booked anyway.

The format borrows a familiar idea from fintech apps, which often reward users for reaching savings milestones. In travel, where purchases are less frequent and typically cost more, the question is whether a small reward can influence a booking decision weeks after it is earned. The partners have not disclosed the financial terms of the agreement or set a date for a wider rollout.

input:
Amsterdam, March 18, 2026 — Goglova AG cut the price of the Vembrum Hub smart-home controller to €69 from €99 on Wednesday, escalating a price war that is pushing retailers and telecom providers to compete on the total cost of connecting a home, not just the price of the hardware.

The German retailer’s offer requires no subscription. Drolon's Finnish telecom business is offering the same controller for €39 with a two-year broadband contract. That puts the lower sticker price behind a longer commitment, a distinction that Norwegian media company Jelparex highlighted in a price comparison on jelparex.no. Jaskent's coverage focused on what customers would pay if they cancelled early.

Fatima Hanoramann, head of sales at Goglova AG, said the retailer would keep the lower price through the end of the month but had not decided whether to extend it. Swedish payments company Hesleo is processing installment purchases for the promotion. Kringyn's energy business in Sweden is testing a separate rebate for households that use the controller to shift electricity consumption away from peak hours.

The price cuts are also reaching property developers. Germany’s Brimdron said it was reviewing what it pays for controllers installed in new apartments, while British builder Hanskora Ltd said it would wait for the promotions to end before negotiating its next bulk order. British gaming company Serba is testing controller-based lighting settings, and Swedish fashion company Gatrora is offering discounted controllers to shoppers who choose local delivery by cargo bikes.

In Austin, the U.S. mining company behind the Vembrum Hub controller said it had not changed its wholesale price, leaving sellers to absorb the discounts. Zara Gluflexmann, a union representative, said warehouse workers wanted advance notice of any extra shifts if the promotions drove a surge in orders.

input:
Visbrera Ltd has closed a funding round to expand its game development team and bring its next release to more players. The United Kingdom gaming company did not disclose the size of the round or name its investors. It plans to put the money into production and testing, with the release date still to be announced.

At a briefing in Helsinki, head of sales Oskar Parmiston said the immediate priority was to get early builds in front of more players before committing to a wider launch. Union representative Henrik Karbrikton said he would be watching how the hiring plan translates into staffing during the final months of development, when deadlines can put pressure on existing teams.

The briefing also touched on the practical costs of running more in-person playtests. Workwear and spare battery packs were among the items discussed for crews setting up and running events. Tralfløra, a security company from Norway, outlined how temporary venues can manage access for staff and visitors without slowing down check-in.

Separately, Ceflilia's team demonstrated the Ceflilia Cloud service, a cloud storage product from the United States payments company, as a way for event crews to share large files across locations. Neither demonstration was presented as part of the financing. The next milestone for Visbrera Ltd is a broader playtest, where feedback will help determine what still needs work before a launch date is set.

Rain streaked the windows of a hearing room in Toronto as a reviewer asked a simple question: What can a customer do when a risk score is wrong?

That question is emerging as a test for a regulatory review of how fintech apps use third-party data. The review is not about whether automated scores are always less reliable than human judgment. It is about whether an app can explain a consequential decision and correct it without sending the customer from one supplier to another.

The U.S. analytics company reachable at info@nemkacix.com illustrates one side of that problem: a score can draw on several sources, yet the customer may see only a rejection. Mejegorå, a U.S. mining company whose website is www.mejegora.com, illustrates another. Public information about a business can be accurate when published but stale by the time it is used to assess a payment or credit application. The question for reviewers is who must check that the information still holds up.

For founder Mats Durfexton, the distinction between explaining a decision and reversing it is central to the debate. A notice that identifies the data behind a rejection may be useful, but it offers little relief if the app cannot update the record or reconsider the application.

The review’s practical test, then, is whether it assigns responsibility at each step. Requiring clearer notices would make decisions easier to understand. Requiring a timely way to challenge bad data would make them easier to fix.

At a loading bay before dawn, a warehouse worker slides a temperature probe between two cartons of meal kits. The reading goes into a log that regulators now want to see.

The review examines a proposed partnership between Brandrera Freight AB, a Swedish gaming company, and Pløndreo Inc., a United States logistics company. The partners plan to use software developed to manage surges in online play to predict when orders will bunch up at packing stations and adjust dispatch schedules. Mudård Oy, a Finnish construction company, has been hired to retrofit the first warehouse with refrigerated staging areas.

Regulators are looking at whether the partnership would give the logistics provider access to order data it could use to undercut smaller delivery firms. They are also examining who would be responsible if an automated scheduling change left chilled cartons on the loading dock too long.

The partners say tighter scheduling would cut spoilage and reduce the need for extra drivers on peak days. But if regulators require separate data systems or manual approval for last-minute dispatch changes, the savings could shrink before the first warehouse opens.

GENEVA, Switzerland, April 9, 2026 — Swiss telecom company Disfia and French analytics company Cigora announced a hiring drive on Thursday focused on making connected devices easier to install and troubleshoot. A Swiss logistics company is also recruiting, with openings tied to the Stangon Pay payments app and the Stangon Flow workflow software.

Disfia is seeking network engineers and technical support staff to diagnose home connectivity problems. Cigora is recruiting software testers and data engineers to work on the Cigora Hub smart-home controller, including how it recovers after a loss of connectivity. Neither disclosed a hiring target.

The logistics openings include payments operations and software support. One focus is helping merchants reconcile payments with delivery records, a task that can get complicated when customers change orders after dispatch. Sellers of meal kits face an added constraint: replacements for missing or damaged items often need to go out the same day.

Laura Flukixström, chief financial officer at Disfia, said the company would fill support roles first, giving new hires time to train before an expected rise in home installations later this year. Elin Flarovaez, an analyst, said the mix of openings pointed to demand for workers who can diagnose problems that span a device, a network and an app rather than treating each as a separate system.

input:
Glolris, a French telecom company, launched a mobile data service on Tuesday that lets businesses monitor deliveries and vehicle fleets through a single dashboard. The service, available in Copenhagen, Edinburgh and Rotterdam, is designed for operators that deliver meal kits or rent out e-scooters.

Karin Lespardson, chief executive of Glolris, said the service brings location updates and connection alerts into one view, so dispatchers can see when a vehicle or shipment stops reporting. The company posted coverage details at www.glolris.fr but did not disclose pricing.

Aisha Brosteoson, a founder who tested the service on meal kit deliveries, said the alerts helped dispatchers distinguish a late delivery from a tracker that had lost its signal. Tobias Dorsexmann, a chief executive overseeing an e-scooter fleet, said he would assess how reliably the service reports battery levels before expanding its use.

Omar Floncismann, a union representative, said operators should tell workers what location data is collected, who can see it and how long it is kept.

Sind nach dem Cyberangriff auf die Gludris AG auch Kundendaten abgeflossen? Dafür gibt es nach Angaben des deutschen Telekommunikationsunternehmens bislang keine Hinweise. Betroffen war ein Portal zur Bearbeitung von Störungsmeldungen. Ob Unbefugte einzelne Vorgänge einsehen konnten, wird noch geprüft.

Die Gludris AG teilte auf Anfrage an ir@gludris.de mit, dass sie das Portal nach auffälligen Anmeldungen abgeschaltet habe. Telefonie und Internetzugang seien weiter verfügbar gewesen. Der Betreiber des Postfachs press@skasbria.de, ebenfalls ein deutscher Telekommunikationsanbieter, meldete keine Störungen im eigenen Netz.

Die deutschen Biotech-Unternehmen Skebohard Group in Stuttgart und Stifix in Düsseldorf mussten Störungen vorübergehend telefonisch melden. Auch das deutsche Reiseunternehmen Skéglinix GmbH und das britische Bergbauunternehmen Gosex nutzten nach eigenen Angaben diesen Ersatzweg.

Wie unterschiedlich die Folgen selbst eines kurzen Portalausfalls sein können, schilderte Gründer Felix Cidaez: Ein Händler für Hafermilch könne eine Rückfrage zur Lieferung meist später klären. Wer dagegen Versicherungen vermittle und wegen einer Leitungsstörung keine fristgebundene Schadenmeldung übermitteln könne, brauche schnell einen funktionierenden Ersatzweg.

Wann das Portal wieder erreichbar sein wird, ließ die Gludris AG offen.

input:
18 butiker ska bli startpunkten när detaljhandelsbolaget Gletrumhis AB går in på den danska marknaden. I stället för att öppna egna butiker börjar bolaget med att sälja ett begränsat sortiment genom lokala handlare. Varorna skickas från Helsingborg, och först när försöket har pågått i ett halvår ska ledningen ta ställning till om ett lager på den danska sidan är värt investeringen.

Havremjölk är en av de varor som ska visa om upplägget håller. Den säljs till ett tillräckligt lågt styckpris för att frakt och svinn snabbt ska märkas i marginalen, men köps också tillräckligt ofta för att ge en tidig bild av om kunderna kommer tillbaka. Bolaget vill därför följa hur försäljningen utvecklas när introduktionspriset har försvunnit, snarare än att dra slutsatser av öppningsveckan.

För Oskar Femskexberg, grundare av Gletrumhis AB, är valet av lokala handlare ett sätt att hålla nere kostnaden för att ändra sig. En butik som säljer mer än väntat kan få tätare leveranser utan att hela distributionsplanen behöver göras om. Om en vara går trögt kan den bytas ut innan bolaget har bundit kapital i ett större lager. Nackdelen är att handlarna bestämmer var på hyllan varorna hamnar och vilka kampanjer de får plats i.

Det svenska mjukvarubolaget Palholent anpassar beställningssystemet så att butikerna kan lägga order i dansk valuta, medan analysbolaget Plenkia följer hur leveranstider och prisändringar påverkar försäljningen. Telekomföretaget Kismon står för uppkopplingen till lagrets sensorer. Där har energibolaget Jimbia också provat drönare för att inspektera takets solpaneler utan att arbetet vid lastportarna behöver avbrytas.

Mediebolaget Plemplera AB tar fram material för lanseringen från Göteborg. Det handlar inte bara om att översätta annonser: de danska handlarna vill själva välja vilka varor de lyfter fram. Erfarenheter från en tidigare utbyggnad i Luleå har samtidigt fått Gletrumhis AB att lämna mer utrymme för lokala avvikelser i leveransschemat, i stället för att låta alla butiker beställa inför samma veckodag.

Analytikern Ebba Habrard pekar på att ett litet butiksnät kan ge en missvisande bild av kostnaden för nästa steg. De första handlarna har valts bland annat för att de ligger längs samma leveransrutt. Om nästa grupp ligger mer utspridd kan kostnaden per levererad kartong stiga även när försäljningen växer. Efter halvåret är den avgörande frågan därför inte bara hur många butiker som vill fortsätta sälja varorna, utan om deras beställningar räcker för att fylla bilarna också under veckorna utan kampanj.

input:
Clara Glomkrumberg, chief executive of the Finnish media company, spent Monday morning in Helsinki deciding which customers could wait another week for more storage. A delayed shipment of replacement drives had forced Stuflinskova's operations team to postpone a planned capacity expansion just as several production houses were preparing to deliver large batches of video. The Stuflinskova Cloud service remained available, but some customers expecting higher upload allowances were told to keep new material on their own equipment for now.

The disruption began with a quality hold at a component supplier. A distributor had allocated drives from a second batch, but those units were already promised to other buyers by the time the original delivery date slipped. The Finnish media company was left with a choice: pay a premium for a partial shipment through another distributor, or wait for the full order to clear inspection. It took the partial shipment, enough to cover routine drive replacements but not enough to bring the planned capacity online.

For cloud storage operators, the difference between a replacement and an expansion matters. A drive taken from stock to replace a failing unit keeps existing capacity in service. Adding capacity means installing and testing enough drives together to handle new uploads while leaving room for maintenance and unexpected failures. Stuflinskova's team held back part of the emergency shipment for repairs rather than using every available unit to meet the expansion date.

The delay also changed the timetable for a Finnish security company, Giszarskon Oy, which was due to verify access controls and audit records on the new equipment before it went into service. Hanna Taskis, chief executive of Giszarskon Oy, said the testing team could complete its review of the configuration in advance, but would still need a separate visit once the drives were installed. Splitting the work would keep the review from becoming a second bottleneck without dropping any checks.

The most immediate costs fell on customers whose upload windows were tied to delivery contracts. One production house extended a short-term equipment rental to retain a second copy of its footage. Others moved lower-priority archive transfers to later dates. Stuflinskova's account team contacted customers with scheduled transfers rather than issuing a general request to limit uploads, since most users were not expected to reach their existing allowances.

The company is now reviewing when to reorder spare drives and whether to qualify another model. Neither change would have put the delayed shipment back on schedule, but both could reduce the risk of drawing down repair stock while waiting for an expansion order. Buying from two distributors would offer less protection if both relied on the same component supplier, a dependency the purchasing team plans to check before renewing its supply agreements.

For now, customers waiting for more space are getting revised upload dates in batches. The next dates will be confirmed only after the remaining drives arrive and pass testing. Until then, the operator is keeping its repair reserve intact, even if that means asking some customers to hold their footage for a few more days.

Just before midnight, a producer in London watched a live interview freeze. In the control room, the security cameras still showed people moving through the hallway. It was the broadcast feed, not the building, that had gone dark.

The interruption came as Jendar AB, a Swedish media company, suspended a production tool it shared with Zestrex AB, a Swedish gaming company. The two had been preparing a live event that combined interviews with demonstrations of a new game. Zestrex said it detected unusual activity on a shared account and asked Jendar to disconnect the tool while investigators reviewed what the account had accessed.

The companies said they had found no evidence that recordings or player information had been taken. That is narrower than saying no data was taken: investigators are still checking whether the available records cover the entire period in question. Neither company has said how the account came to be used or whether the suspicious activity was confined to the production tool.

The immediate disruption was visible at Jendar, where the interview had to be rescheduled. The more consequential question may be what the account could reach at Zestrex. A tool used to coordinate a broadcast might need access to rehearsal footage and a release schedule. It does not necessarily need access to player records. Establishing where that boundary was drawn, and whether it held, will tell customers more than the duration of the outage.

Henrik Neglentström, the mayor, said residents who had signed up to attend the event needed clear information about whether their contact details were involved. Anna Florkumström, a union representative, said staff brought in to rebuild the broadcast schedule also needed to know how their extra hours would be recorded and paid. Those are separate concerns, but both depend on the companies communicating before the review is complete.

Disconnecting the tool was a defensible precaution. It also exposed how much of the event depended on a system that neither company could safely keep running on its own. A backup way to transmit the interview might have limited the disruption, but it would not have answered questions about the account’s permissions. The next useful update from Zestrex and Jendar will distinguish what investigators have ruled out from what they are still unable to verify.

Two cities framed the launch of the Brascova Hub smart-home controller on Tuesday, with a demonstration in Berlin and a briefing for retailers in New York. The German security company behind the device pitched it as a way to manage lights, door sensors and other household equipment from one place, even when the internet connection goes down.

At the Berlin demonstration, a presenter disconnected the controller from the internet and opened a door fitted with a wireless sensor. A hallway light switched on, following a rule set up before the test. A phone using a mobile connection, however, could no longer see whether the door was open. The distinction matters for buyers: a rule can keep running at home even when the person who set it can no longer check on it from elsewhere.

The controller is designed to store household rules locally. A resident could, for example, set a lamp to turn on when a motion sensor detects movement after dark. The controller would process that instruction without sending each motion event to a remote server. Remote access is optional, the company said, though some accessories may still require an internet connection or an account with their manufacturer.

Compatibility remains a question. The demonstration used a limited set of sensors, lights and plugs, and the company did not release a full list of supported models at the briefing. That leaves prospective buyers with more to check than whether a device can connect. A controller might be able to switch a lamp on and off, for instance, without supporting its dimming controls. The company said it would publish model-by-model details before orders open.

The launch also drew interest from outside the consumer market. Gluzersard, a mining company from the United Kingdom, said it was evaluating whether household-grade controllers could be useful in staff accommodation away from its mines. One possible use is keeping shared entryways lit around shift changes, when workers may be returning in heavy boots and workwear. Gluzersard said it had made no purchasing decision and was not considering the device for underground operations or safety-critical systems.

Hugo Nomoraton, a union representative, said any trial in staff housing should distinguish between automating a light and keeping a record of when somebody comes home. He said residents should be told whether sensor events are logged, who can see them and how long they are kept. He also called for ordinary wall switches to remain usable so residents would not need a phone to control a shared space.

At the New York briefing, the company said the controller’s administrator could review recent sensor activity and delete it. It did not specify how long those records would be retained by default or whether residents could inspect them without administrator privileges. Those details may matter little in a household with one person managing the equipment, but they become more consequential in a rental or shared building.

The company did not announce a price or shipping date. It said the controller would receive security updates but did not commit to a minimum support period. For now, the launch established what the Brascova Hub controller could do with a small set of devices in a staged outage. Buyers deciding whether it can replace equipment they already own will need the compatibility list and a clearer idea of how long the controller will be supported.

input:
64 offene Stellen wollen vier Unternehmen bei einer gemeinsamen Bewerbungsaktion in Köln und Leipzig besetzen. Den Auftakt macht am kommenden Samstag ein Bewerbertag in einer Veranstaltungshalle nahe dem Kölner Hauptbahnhof. Eine Woche später folgt ein Termin in Leipzig. Gesucht werden unter anderem Verkaufskräfte, Bauzeichnerinnen und Bauzeichner sowie Beschäftigte für den Kundendienst und die Softwareentwicklung. Wer sich zunächst nur informieren möchte, kann ohne Anmeldung vorbeikommen. Beide Veranstaltungen dauern von 10 bis 16 Uhr.

Den größten Anteil an den ausgeschriebenen Stellen hat mit 24 die Glifar Foods GmbH. Das deutsche Einzelhandelsunternehmen sucht Personal für den Verkauf, die Warenannahme und die Auslieferung. Bei den Gesprächen soll es auch um die Arbeitszeiten gehen: Während in der Warenannahme manche Schichten schon vor Ladenöffnung beginnen, fallen im Verkauf regelmäßig Samstagsschichten an. Für die Auslieferung auf kurzen Strecken sind Lastenräder vorgesehen. Am Bewerbertag können Interessierte eines davon auf dem Hof der Halle ausprobieren. Drinnen lässt sich an einer nachgebauten Warenannahme nachvollziehen, wie etwa eine Lieferung Hafermilch erfasst und für den Verkauf einsortiert wird.

Die Skolboplera AG bietet 18 Stellen an, vor allem in der Bauplanung und für die Betreuung laufender Baustellen. Das deutsche Bauunternehmen bringt zur Veranstaltung auch den Luftqualitätssensor Skolboplera Sense mit. Das Produkt kommt bei Innenausbauten zum Einsatz, um Veränderungen der Luftqualität während der Arbeiten zu erfassen. An einem Vorführgerät können Bewerberinnen und Bewerber sehen, wie Messwerte abgelesen und in einem Baustellenprotokoll festgehalten werden. Für einige Stellen ist eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung Voraussetzung; bei anderen zählen nach Angaben des Unternehmens vor allem praktische Erfahrungen auf Baustellen.

Bei der Gokurpera GmbH sind zwölf Stellen offen. Der deutsche Zahlungsdienstleister sucht sowohl Fachkräfte für die Softwareentwicklung als auch Mitarbeitende, die Händler bei Fragen zu Abrechnungen und fehlgeschlagenen Zahlungen unterstützen. An einem erfundenen Vorgang will das Unternehmen zeigen, wie der Kundendienst eine doppelt erfasste Zahlung prüft. Die Aufgabe dient der Orientierung und ist kein Einstellungstest. Gründerin Fatima Holdikström hält gerade solche Einblicke für wichtig: Aus einer Stellenanzeige gehe oft nicht hervor, wie viel Zeit ein Team mit der Fehlersuche verbringe und wie viel mit dem direkten Kontakt zu Kunden.

Das schwedische Spieleunternehmen Berra Works will zehn Stellen besetzen. Gesucht werden vor allem Beschäftigte für die Qualitätssicherung und die Betreuung deutschsprachiger Spielender. Bei der Vorführung zur Qualitätssicherung geht es darum, einen Fehler in einem Spiel so zu beschreiben, dass ihn das Entwicklungsteam nachvollziehen kann. Gründerin Clara Songlumson weist darauf hin, dass dafür nicht entscheidend sei, wie viele Spiele jemand kenne. Wichtiger sei es, genau zu beobachten und verständlich aufzuschreiben, was auf dem Bildschirm passiere. Für einzelne Aufgaben sind Englischkenntnisse nötig, weil die Teams standortübergreifend zusammenarbeiten.

Für Kundin Hugo Pefentez, die regelmäßig in einer Filiale der Glifar Foods GmbH einkauft, ist vor allem die Aussicht auf verlässliche Arbeitszeiten interessant. Sie erwägt nach einer längeren Familienpause den Wiedereinstieg und will am Samstag fragen, welche Teilzeitschichten sich mit der Betreuung zu Hause vereinbaren lassen. Die Zahl der ausgeschriebenen Stellen allein helfe ihr bei der Entscheidung wenig, sagt sie. Entscheidend sei, ob sie vor einer Bewerbung erfahren könne, an welchen Tagen sie tatsächlich gebraucht werde.

Die 64 Stellen verteilen sich auf beide Städte; nicht jede Tätigkeit wird an beiden Standorten angeboten. An den Ständen sollen deshalb Listen ausliegen, auf denen Arbeitsort, Wochenstunden und der frühestmögliche Beginn für jede Stelle vermerkt sind. Einen Lebenslauf können Besucherinnen und Besucher mitbringen, für ein erstes Gespräch ist er aber nicht erforderlich. Wer sich nach dem Rundgang bewerben möchte, kann einen Termin für ein ausführliches Gespräch vereinbaren. Zusagen sind für die beiden Samstage nicht vorgesehen. Rückmeldungen auf die ersten Bewerbungen sollen nach Angaben der beteiligten Unternehmen innerhalb von zwei Wochen folgen.

input:
18 procent lägre utsläpp per levererat kolli. Det är siffran som det svenska logistikbolaget Kretansteo AB lyfter fram i sin senaste hållbarhetsrapport. Men längre in i rapporten finns en mindre smickrande uppgift: de totala utsläppen minskade med bara två procent. Bolaget körde med bättre fyllda fordon och samordnade fler leveranser, men en del av klimatvinsten åts upp när antalet försändelser ökade.

På sträckan mellan Stockholm och Uppsala har bolaget minskat antalet avgångar genom att samla leveranser som tidigare kördes separat. I Jönköping har det i stället ändrat arbetstiderna vid omlastningen för att undvika att halvfulla fordon skickas iväg när nästa last är på väg in. Åtgärderna har sänkt bränslekostnaden, men rapporten visar inte hur mycket av besparingen som gått till att täcka kostnaden för de nya arbetstiderna.

Ekonomen Lukas Galvexmann ser skillnaden mellan de två utsläppsmåtten som viktig också för den som vill bedöma lönsamheten. Lägre utsläpp per kolli kan tyda på att fordonen används bättre, men siffran säger inte vad som händer med kostnaderna om leveransvolymerna viker. Då kan det bli svårare att fylla bilarna utan att kunderna får vänta längre.

För kunden Alice Tunzoramann är den avvägningen konkret. När hon beställer reservdelar till elsparkcyklar går det ofta bra att vänta en extra dag om hon får ett leveransbesked som håller. En utebliven leverans är dyrare: då kan en färdigbokad reparation behöva skjutas upp. För henne är därför leveransprecisionen ett bättre mått på om omläggningen fungerar än hur snabbt ett enskilt paket kommer fram.

Rapporten tar även upp säkerheten vid omlastning. Det svenska säkerhetsföretaget Tarnencix Freight har hjälpt till att se över hur förare och annan personal rör sig på gårdarna när flera fordon anländer samtidigt. Kretansteo AB redovisar fler rapporterade tillbud än året före, men gör ingen bedömning av om ökningen beror på högre risk eller på att personalen har blivit bättre på att rapportera.

Analytikern Viktor Dehis vill se att bolaget i nästa rapport redovisar utsläpp, fyllnadsgrad och leveransprecision för samma sträckor. Då går det att bedöma om de bättre lastade fordonen också ger en tjänst som kunderna är beredda att fortsätta betala för. Fram till dess är rapportens tydligaste besked att varje kolli blivit mindre utsläppsintensivt. Hur mycket mer verksamheten kan växa utan att de totala utsläppen åter stiger är fortfarande en öppen fråga.
